data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism's concluding sentence — 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all' — is a non-sequitur that contradicts the claim it is supposed to support. The claim defends a preference 'on Popper's terms,' which is precisely an appeal to the structural features of Popper's methodology (severity of tests, empirical content, corroboration). If the underlying structure is irrelevant to the outcome, then the Popperian framing is also irrelevant, and the claim's own justification collapses. Nothing in the preceding reframing — from probabilistic truth-judgment to methodological choice — entails that structure is irrelevant; the entire argument depends on the Popperian structure being the thing that makes the preference rational. The sentence is either an unearned assertion or smuggles in a conclusion that refutes the claim.
